column3: It closely repeats the created heavens and earth, descending water, and divinely produced varied growth that ground the focus argument.
Earth as human origin, return, and emergence extends the Creator's power beyond the garden scene to life and resurrection.
Its rain-to-diverse-vegetation sequence closely supports the focus's visible productive order, though it lacks the challenge about rival gods.
It combines earth and sky, rain, fruit-provision, and the prohibition of setting equals beside God in an especially close parallel.
The next challenge in the same series shifts from gardens to earth's stability, rivers, and sea barriers while retaining the rival-god question.
Creator of earth and high heavens supports the source of the focus's order, but the verse concerns revelation rather than water and growth.
It restates creation, rain, fruit provision, and rivers, adding an extended account of the provision flowing from the same Creator.
Within the same challenge sequence, origination, renewal, and provision from sky and earth directly reinforce exclusive divine agency.
The direct contrast between one who creates and one who cannot create clarifies the focus's rejection of divine equals.
Blessed water descending from heaven and producing gardens and harvest is a direct, compact parallel to the focus's garden evidence.
Storehouses of the land and administrative custodianship add no material connection to creation, rain, or gardens.
Creation of heavens and earth followed by condemnation of those who equate others with their Lord reinforces the focus's closing polemic.
It expands the focus's rain-and-growth sign into a wider ordered network of creation, transport, winds, and clouds.
The adjacent challenge links God alone with answering distress and making successors on earth, extending the series' exclusive-agency claim.
Creation, proportioning, and balancing offer a general account of deliberate divine formation without the focus's natural sequence.
Rain becoming drink, pasture, and trees directly develops the focus's claim that God alone brings forth trees through water.
The exposed, sick figure supplies only a remote background for the following divinely grown plant.
Its command to uphold justice has only a distant verbal resonance with the focus's condemnation of false equalizing.
The adjacent challenge invokes guidance and winds before mercy, contributing a neighboring stage of the water-and-provision signs.
Divine bounty and human ingratitude summarize the response appropriate to the focus's displayed provision without adding its mechanism.
Creation and resurrection as easy as one soul broaden divine power but do not illuminate the rain-and-garden argument.
God's causing a tree to grow for Jonah provides a concrete instance of divine tree-producing agency.
The same local sequence identifies prior worship of other than God as an obstacle, sharpening the focus's anti-association conclusion.
Descent from the Lord of the worlds concerns revelation, not the created water-and-growth order.
The rain that stirs dead earth into varied beautiful growth gives a detailed life-producing parallel to the focus's gardens.
The heavens and earth not weeping over Pharaoh's people do not add to the focus's creation and provision argument.
The repeated descent of the Quran is a distinct kind of descent and adds little to the focus's rain imagery.
God's bringing forth grain is a direct but narrower instance of the focus's divinely produced vegetation.
This nearby dispute over omens locates rejection in the same surah but adds little to the creation proof.
Mary's divinely caused growth and unaccounted provision give a personal-scale instance of sustenance beyond human control.
Its dense gardens name the same visible product featured in the focus, though without the causal argument.
The Creator's beginning and restoration of creation support the exclusive divine capacity developed by the surrounding challenges.
The bare assertion that humans were created supports the focus's source claim but adds no specific sign.
The description of transgressors offers no substantive connection to creation, water, or gardens.
The adjacent statement about blindness concerning the hereafter supplies only the broader setting of failed recognition.
The demand that an angel descend with the messenger concerns a different objection and descent.
Gardens and grapevines provide a direct image of the delightful cultivated abundance named in the focus.
Its challenge whether alleged partners can originate and restore creation closely matches the focus's question about a god beside God.
It directly joins creation of the earth with rebuking those who assign equals to its Creator.
Polemical argument over deities in another dispute supplies no useful connection to the focus's natural signs.
The command to submit belongs to the same surah episode but does not develop the focus's creation argument.
Calling humans to consider their origin reinforces the focus's invitation to reason from created evidence.
The ethical rebuke concerning spouses does not clarify the focus's account of rain, gardens, or rivals.
The comparison between the One who guides and helpless false guides parallels the focus's rhetorical test of alleged partners.
Creation of heavens and earth as signs supports the focus's appeal to cosmic observation, though it is less specific than earlier parallels.
Guiding and judging by truth only distantly echoes the focus's final criticism of distorted equalizing.
The immediately preceding destructive rain forms a purposeful contrast with the life-giving rain of the focus.
Descent of clear verses is a separate divine sign and has limited bearing on rain-fed gardens.
The spread earth, set mountains, and beautiful paired growth closely support the focus's display of ordered vegetation.
Succession on earth concerns human testing rather than the focus's argument from natural provision.
Creation of heavens and earth in truth makes the focus's visible order an evidentiary sign, though without its water sequence.
A community that guides and judges justly has only a distant resonance with the focus's charge of false equivalence.
The opening travel scene of Moses does not add to the focus's proof from creation.
Reflection on how a camel was created is a broad analogous call to observe creation, but adds no shared scene.
The patterned sky alone does not materially develop the focus's rain, growth, or anti-association argument.
Destruction of earlier wrongdoers is unrelated to the focus's natural proof.
Worship of the Creator follows from creation generally, but this adds little after the closer creation-and-rain parallels.
The sky with constellations offers no focused connection to water, gardens, or divine rivals.
The nearby denial of resurrection reflects the surrounding failure to recognize divine power but not the garden sign itself.
The request for earth-grown foods mentions vegetation but serves a distinct narrative of dissatisfaction and disobedience.
The tree of Zaqqam is a contrasting tree image, not evidence of life-giving provision.
God's originating and restoring creation supports the same exclusive creative power, though it turns toward judgment.
Earth's production of many noble pairs is a close natural-sign parallel to the focus's beautiful gardens.
The Maker of heavens and earth is presented as the obvious ground against doubt, reinforcing the focus's rhetorical appeal.
The adjacent assertion of God's exclusive unseen knowledge continues the surah's exclusivity theme without the focus's creation sign.
The descent upon those who divided revelation does not illuminate the water-and-garden sequence.
The earth's splitting supplies a concise physical counterpart to emergence and germination from the ground.
Delivery of Solomon's letter and awaiting a reply are unrelated to the focus's divine-creation proof.
Creation from nothing supports the focus's contrast between divine creative power and human inability.
Its question whether humans or God produced the tree directly echoes the focus's declaration that humans cannot grow its trees.
Rain from heaven making the earth green gives a direct parallel and adds the divine subtlety behind the visible transformation.
The seven paths above and continued care for creation offer only a broad cosmic frame for the focus's heavens-and-earth claim.
The sky splitting at the fulfilled promise does not add to the focus's life-giving water imagery.
The test involving the altered throne belongs to the same narrative but not the focus's natural-sign argument.
The rival materials of fire and clay concern an arrogant comparison rather than the focus's account of creation and gardens.
The challenge over who can provide if God withholds provision reinforces the focus's claim that provision is exclusively God's.
Rain reviving a dead land as provision directly extends the focus's growth result and points to further life-giving power.
Descent of a merciful revelation is only loosely analogous to water descending for growth.
The descent of scripture to judge disputes is distinct from the focus's natural evidence and adds little here.
Recognition of the throne in Solomon's narrative does not clarify the focus's creation proof.
Creation of a human from clay is a broad origin statement without the focus's water, vegetation, or rival-god contrast.
Its rejection of unsupported witnesses against God only remotely supports the focus's challenge to claims about other gods.
Rules for replacing compromised witnesses do not contribute to the focus's natural or theological argument.
The Creator who also guides presents creation as continuing divine care, complementing the focus's ordered provision.
The fueled fire has no useful relation to the focus's heavens, rain, or gardens.
Deliverance of believers in the same surah contrasts with prior punishment but does not explain the focus's garden sign.
Creation of spouses as a sign broadens the category of divine signs but is remote from the focus's natural sequence.
Divine presence with the mindful and excellent does not clarify the focus's creative proof.
The procedural account of truthful testimony is unrelated to the focus's water and vegetation argument.
Creation of an individual alone humbles human self-sufficiency but has little direct connection to the focus's displayed order.
The hypothetical effects of a Quran and God's total command do not materially develop the focus's natural sign.
Human creation from clay supports divine formation in general but adds no rain, growth, or anti-association dimension.
The rebuke of a people boasting in strength recalls that their Creator is stronger, supporting the focus's Creator-versus-creature contrast.
Calling people to fear the Creator of them and earlier generations gives a general source-based admonition only.
The descent of security after battle is unrelated to the focus's life-giving descent of water.
A request for a blessed landing uses descent as arrival and offers only a remote resonance with provision.
Inheritance apportionment does not contribute to the focus's argument from creation, rain, or gardens.
The reply to demands for signs distinguishes their divine source, but it is not a close parallel to the focus's sign.
The expulsion of a hostile group and the call to take warning do not illuminate the focus passage.
Human weakness explains legal easing and offers only a distant reminder of creaturely limitation before the Creator.
Water sent down from heaven produces vegetation, grain, and gardens; it is one of the closest omitted parallels to the focus's full sequence.
Winds, clouds, and rain revive a dead land and yield every kind of fruit, directly extending the focus's life-giving water sign.
The spread earth, rivers, mountains, and paired fruits make the focus's garden a sign within a broader ordered terrestrial design.
Neighboring garden plots, vines, crops, and palms watered by one water show differentiated growth under one divine ordering.
God spreads the earth, fixes mountains, and grows every balanced thing, supplying a close framework for the focus's measured gardens.
Fertilizing winds and water sent down from heaven explicitly deny human possession of the life-giving supply behind the focus's trees.
The rain by which God grows crops, olives, dates, grapes, and every fruit directly details the focus's claim of divinely produced trees.
Water sent from heaven revives the earth after its death, giving a concise and direct statement of the focus's productive order.
The earth's plants are presented as provision for humans and animals, developing the purpose of the focus's garden growth.
Making every living thing from water supplies the wider life principle behind the focus's rain-fed gardens.
Water is sent down in measure and settled in the earth, specifying the controlled provision that precedes the focus's growth.
Water then produces gardens of palms and vines with abundant fruit, an especially close omitted counterpart to the focus.
Winds announce mercy before pure water descends from heaven, supplying the antecedent stage of the focus's garden sign.
The water gives life to dead land and provides drink, directly explaining the productive and sustaining outcome in the focus.
God sends water from heaven, revives the earth, and makes this a sign for people who understand, closely matching the focus's appeal.
Water is driven to barren land so crops emerge for people and livestock, strongly paralleling the focus's growth beyond human power.
Winds drive clouds and rain revives dead earth; this is a direct parallel that also links the sign to resurrection.
The dead earth is revived and grain is brought from it, presenting the same divine bringing-forth process in compact form.
Gardens of palms and vines with flowing springs provide a direct garden-and-water complement to the focus.
Water descends, enters springs in the earth, and produces varied crops, making explicit the hidden route from heaven to growth.
The lifeless earth stirs and swells when water descends, directly displaying the transformation presupposed by the focus's gardens.
Water descends in due measure and revives a dead land, closely joining measured provision and emergence.
The earth is laid out for creatures with fruit, palms, grain, and fragrant plants, broadening the focus's provision imagery.
The question whether humans cause what they sow to grow directly parallels the focus's declaration that humans cannot grow its trees.
God's claim that He is the grower sharpens the focus's contrast between divine agency and human inability.
God revives the earth after death, preserving the focus's vegetation sign as a repeated proof of life-giving power.
Abundant heavenly rain is promised as divine provision, supplying a clear rain source for the focus's garden imagery.
The promised rain is joined to wealth, children, gardens, and rivers, closely matching the focus's provision through water.
Abundant water poured from rain clouds directly supplies the focus's heavenly-water premise.
The water brings forth grain and plants, a close parallel to the focus's divinely produced vegetation.
Lush gardens follow the rain and growth sequence, directly echoing the focus's delightful gardens.
The command to consider food introduces the same observational argument from provision that the focus makes through gardens.
Water poured down abundantly supplies the first stage of the focus's rain-to-growth sequence.
Earth split open supplies the receiving and emergence stage that complements the focus's trees growing from watered land.
Grapes and fodder extend the specific plant products produced by the divine process described in the focus.
Olives and palms name trees that make the focus's claim about human inability to grow trees concrete.
Fruit and pasture state the provision resulting from the same water, earth, and growth sequence.
These provisions are explicitly for humans and livestock, clarifying the beneficial end of the focus's gardens.
The sky characterized by returning rain provides a compact cosmic source for the focus's descending water.
Gardens, palms, crops, and fruits are enumerated as divine produce, extending the focus's tree-and-garden evidence into accountable provision.
Good land produces vegetation by its Lord's permission while bad land yields scant growth, directly qualifying the focus's divine growth claim.
Rain makes the earth's vegetation flourish and adorn itself before it passes away, a vivid close parallel to the focus's water-fed growth.
The promise of plentiful heavenly rain presents rain as a divine gift and reinforces the focus's dependence of growth on God.
Rain from heaven turns vegetation into temporary growth, providing a contrasting reminder of the garden scene's transience.
Cloud formation, hail, and lightning map the heavenly water system that precedes the focus's rain and vegetation.
The question who creates the heavens and earth and sends water to revive the earth closely restates the focus's proof and its answer.
Winds form and spread clouds before rain descends and revives the earth, directly filling out the focus's rain-to-life process.
Two gardens as a sign of provision show the beneficial result of divine endowment, though the verse does not state the rain process.
Water descending from heaven produces varied fruits, making a direct compact parallel to the focus's productive rain.
Rain is sent after despair and spread as mercy, reinforcing the focus's water as purposeful divine provision.
Rain revives the earth after death as a sign for reasoning people, closely supporting the focus's observational argument.
The challenge over who can restore flowing water underscores human dependence on the water source behind the focus's gardens.
Water brought forth from a rock at God's command provides a distinct direct instance of divine control over life-sustaining water.
God's splitting of grain and date stones into living growth offers a close complementary sign of plant emergence beyond human origination.
The Creator of heavens and earth is explicitly able to recreate humans, extending the focus's creative proof to restoration.
The two gardens' unfailing yield and inner river provide a garden image, but as a parable it is less direct than the natural-sign passages.
The ripe palm providing dates is a provision image, though it does not make the focus's claim about the originating growth process.
Human creation from water broadens water's life-giving role but is remote from the focus's heavenly water and gardens.
The One who makes fire available from a green tree demonstrates transformative creative power through the very tree imagery central to the focus.
Earth made as a resting place and pathways prepared for guidance supplies the terrestrial setting completed by the rain in the next verse.
Fruit and date palms with sheaths extend the focus's trees into a broader inventory of divine terrestrial provision.
Firm mountains and fresh water placed on earth provide an ordered-land and water counterpart to the focus's garden setting.
